definitions.explanation: An artificial or stocked pond where customers pay to fish, typically for koi, carp, trout, or other freshwater fish. A popular leisure facility for families and casual anglers.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもと{釣|つ}り{堀|ぼり}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to a fishing pond with my child.

examples.japanese: {釣|つ}り{堀|ぼり}では{初心者|しょしんしゃ}でも{気軽|きがる}に{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: Even beginners can casually enjoy fishing at a pay-to-fish pond.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}の{釣|つ}り{堀|ぼり}では、{釣|つ}った{魚|さかな}をその{場|ば}で{焼|や}いて{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: At the neighborhood fishing pond, you can grill and eat the fish you catch on the spot.

notes:
Compound of {釣|つ}り (fishing) + {堀|ほり} (pond, moat). The reading of {堀|ほり} shifts to ぼり due to rendaku.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {釣|つ}り{堀|ぼり}に{行|い}く: to go to a fishing pond
- {釣|つ}り{堀|ぼり}で{釣|つ}る: to fish at a fishing pond
- {室内|しつない}{釣|つ}り{堀|ぼり}: indoor fishing pond
- {鯉|こい}の{釣|つ}り{堀|ぼり}: carp fishing pond

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
A popular casual leisure activity, especially with families and groups. Equipment is rented on-site, and fees are typically based on time or per fish caught. Common targets include {鯉|こい} (carp), {鮒|ふな} (crucian carp), and {鱒|ます} (trout).
